title.narrative: A Path to the Phased Elimination of Malaria from Bangladesh - Bangladesh (01-Jan-2021-31-Dec-2023)

description.narrative: Bangladesh, Malaria, Economic Relations Division, Ministry of Finance of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (MOF Bangladesh)This program has the following goals: By 2025, reduce malaria annual parasite incidence (API) to less than 1 per 1,000 population at risk in CHT districts, interrupt local transmission and eliminate indigenous malaria in phased manner in 10 other endemic districts, determine malaria-free status of remaining 51 districts.. The objectives of this program are: To develop an integrated disease surveillance system, especially for climate-sensitive priority diseases, ensuring linkage with community-based surveillance systems. To identify an EWARS platform for data analysis, risk prediction, and early warning, in close coordination with existing climate services. To integrate relevant meteorological, climate, and environmental data into the integrated disease surveillance system. To determine future needs to scale up the EWARS at the National level. To develop/ scale up geo-referenced health management information system for climate induced diseases and risk factors. Establish and enhance surveillance systems for priority vector-borne and climate-induced diseases including HIV, TB, and Malaria for key and vulnerable population. Strengthen capacity of public health facility and community health workforce on climate-induced diseases to improve early detection, risk mitigation, and patient referral processes.. Mobilise communities through social mobilisation campaigns, involving local leaders, youth platforms, and religious figures to raise awareness about climate-sensitive health risks, promote preventive measures, and encourage proactive health-seeking behaviours.. Implement mass awareness initiatives including clean-up campaigns, to promote climate-sensitive health practices and reduce the burden of vector-borne diseases
